title: Jeremiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 47 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 47.

questions.question: Who received the word of the LORD against the Philistines in Jeremiah 47?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah the prophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:1 states that the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47, who smote Gaza before this prophecy?
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:1 mentions that the prophecy came before Pharaoh smote Gaza.

questions.question: From which direction do the waters rise up as an overflowing flood in Jeremiah 47?
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the north
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 says, 'waters rise up out of the north' as an overflowing flood.

questions.question: What will the overflowing flood do to the land according to Jeremiah 47?
options: Overflow the land and all that is therein
questions.correctAnswer: Overflow the land and all that is therein
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 states the flood shall overflow the land and all that is therein.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 47, what is the reaction of the men and inhabitants when the flood comes?
options: The men shall cry and all inhabitants shall howl
They will flee to the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: The men shall cry and all inhabitants shall howl
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 says the men shall cry and all inhabitants of the land shall howl.

questions.question: What causes the noise described in Jeremiah 47:3?
options: Stamping of the hoofs of strong horses, rushing chariots, rumbling wheels
questions.correctAnswer: Stamping of the hoofs of strong horses, rushing chariots, rumbling wheels
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:3 describes the noise coming from the stamping of hoofs, rushing chariots, and rumbling wheels.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47, what will the fathers fail to do because of feebleness of hands?
questions.correctAnswer: Look back to their children
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:3 states that fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands.

questions.question: True or False: The prophecy in Jeremiah 47 was delivered after Pharaoh smote Gaza.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:1 clearly says the prophecy came before Pharaoh smote Gaza.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 47 describes the flood waters as coming from the south.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 states the waters rise up out of the north, not the south.

questions.question: True or False: The inhabitants of the land shall howl when the overflowing flood comes according to Jeremiah 47.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 says all the inhabitants of the land shall howl at the coming flood.

questions.question: True or False: The noise of horses and chariots is described in Jeremiah 47 as a sign of joy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:3 describes the noise of horses and chariots in a context of fear and distress, not joy.

questions.question: What comes first according to Jeremiah 47:2-3?
options: Waters rising out of the north
questions.correctAnswer: Waters rising out of the north
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 starts with the waters rising out of the north before mentioning the cries and noises in verse 3.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47:4, which cities are mentioned as having their helpers cut off?
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus and Zidon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 mentions Tyrus and Zidon as losing every helper that remaineth.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47:5, which city is described as having baldness come upon it?
questions.correctAnswer: Gaza
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:5 states that baldness is come upon Gaza.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47:6, what is the LORD's sword told to do?
options: Put up into the scabbard, rest, and be still
questions.correctAnswer: Put up into the scabbard, rest, and be still
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:6 asks the sword of the LORD how long it will be before it is quiet and tells it to put itself into the scabbard and rest.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 47 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47:4, what will happen to the Philistines and their allies?
options: They will be spoiled and cut off from their helpers
They will conquer Tyrus and Zidon
They will form a strong alliance with Caphtor
They will receive blessings from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will be spoiled and cut off from their helpers
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 states that the day will come to spoil all the Philistines and cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth, showing God's judgment on them.

questions.question: What imagery does Jeremiah 47:5 use to describe the condition of Gaza?
options: Gaza is covered in lush vineyards
Gaza is fortified with strong walls
questions.correctAnswer: Baldness has come upon Gaza
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:5 uses the metaphor of baldness upon Gaza to indicate desolation and mourning, reflecting the dire judgment coming upon the city.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 47:6, the 'sword of the LORD' is told to be still. What practical lesson about trust in God can be drawn from this?
options: Patience and trust in God’s timing are essential
One should always be ready for battle
questions.correctAnswer: Patience and trust in God’s timing are essential
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:6 personifies the sword of the LORD and commands it to rest and be still, teaching believers to trust God's timing and have patience in His plans.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 47:4-5 together illustrate the consequences of sin and disobedience?
options: They reveal that destruction and desolation follow rebellion against God
They promise restoration and peace for the Philistines
They encourage building alliances for protection
They suggest that mourning will bring immediate healing
questions.correctAnswer: They reveal that destruction and desolation follow rebellion against God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 speaks of spoiling the Philistines and cutting off helpers, while verse 5 describes the desolation of Gaza and Ashkelon, showing the dire results of turning away from God.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 47:6 teach about the role of divine instruments like the 'sword of the LORD'?
options: They act according to God’s command and rest when ordered
They act independently of God’s will
They symbolize human weapons of war
They are always silent and inactive
questions.correctAnswer: They act according to God’s command and rest when ordered
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:6 shows the sword of the LORD being told to put itself up into the scabbard and rest, indicating divine instruments obey God's timing and authority.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 47:7, why will the 'sword of the LORD' not be quiet?
options: Because the LORD has given it a charge against Ashkelon and the seashore
Because it wants to rest and be still
Because it has been defeated in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD has given it a charge against Ashkelon and the seashore
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:7 explains that the sword cannot be quiet because the LORD has appointed it a charge to execute judgment on Ashkelon and the seashore.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'how long wilt thou cut thyself?' in Jeremiah 47:5 imply about the Philistines’ actions?
options: They are engaging in self-inflicted mourning or suffering
They are preparing for a joyful festival
They are planting crops for the future
questions.correctAnswer: They are engaging in self-inflicted mourning or suffering
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:5 uses the expression 'how long wilt thou cut thyself?' which refers to a mourning ritual involving self-harm, showing their grief and desperation.

questions.question: How can Jeremiah 47:4-6 teach a believer about humility and surrender to God’s will?
options: By showing that God’s judgment is inevitable and we must submit
By encouraging self-reliance in times of trouble
By promising that human strength will overcome adversity
By suggesting that ignoring God’s commands leads to peace
questions.correctAnswer: By showing that God’s judgment is inevitable and we must submit
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 depict God's judgment as certain and powerful, reminding believers that humility and submission to God’s will are necessary responses.

questions.question: A fellow believer feels overwhelmed by trials as described in Jeremiah 47:4. What biblical truth from this passage would best encourage them?
options: God’s sovereign judgment is purposeful and will bring justice
Trials are a sign of abandonment by God
Human helpers are more reliable than God
One should try to avoid all difficulties
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign judgment is purposeful and will bring justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 reveals that God’s judgment is intentional and just, encouraging believers to trust in His sovereignty even during hardships.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 47:2 describes the waters rising up out of the south as a metaphor for destruction.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 says the waters rise up out of the north, not the south, symbolizing an overwhelming flood of destruction from that direction.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 47:3 mentions that fathers will look back to their children for help during the coming destruction.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:3 states that fathers shall not look back to their children for help due to feebleness of hands, highlighting helplessness in the face of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 47:6 calls the sword of the LORD to be still, teaching us the importance of resting in God's timing.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:6 personifies the sword of the LORD and commands it to rest and be still, teaching believers to trust in God's timing and rest in His sovereign plan.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'remnant of the country of Caphtor' mentioned in Jeremiah 47:4?
options: They are the remaining Philistines subject to God's judgment
They are allies who will defeat the Philistines
They are a peaceful tribe unaffected by conflict
They are the builders of Tyrus and Zidon
questions.correctAnswer: They are the remaining Philistines subject to God's judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 identifies the remnant of Caphtor as part of the Philistine people who will be spoiled by God’s judgment, emphasizing the comprehensive nature of His justice.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 47:5's mention of Ashkelon being 'cut off with the remnant of their valley' relate to the overall message of the chapter?
options: It signifies total destruction and loss among the Philistines
It promises future prosperity for Ashkelon
It indicates a military alliance forming
It describes a natural disaster unrelated to judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies total destruction and loss among the Philistines
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:5 highlights the severe consequences for Ashkelon and surrounding areas, reinforcing the chapter’s theme of divine judgment on the Philistine cities.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 47:6 imply about the tension between divine judgment and divine mercy?
options: That even instruments of judgment are commanded to rest, implying mercy follows judgment
That judgment is endless and without pause
That mercy is not mentioned or considered
That humans control when judgment occurs
questions.correctAnswer: That even instruments of judgment are commanded to rest, implying mercy follows judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 6 commands the sword of the LORD to be still and rest, suggesting that judgment is not perpetual and that mercy or peace may eventually follow God's discipline.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 47.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47:7, why can the sword of the LORD not be quiet?
options: Because the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon and the sea shore
Because the Philistines continue to rebel
Because Gaza has not been spoiled
Because the remnant of Caphtor is still strong
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon and the sea shore
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:7 states the sword cannot be quiet because the LORD has given it a charge against Ashkelon and the sea shore, appointing it specifically for this purpose.

questions.question: What historical event is referenced as occurring before the prophecy against the Philistines in Jeremiah 47:1?
options: The Israelites entered the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh smote Gaza
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:1 clearly states the prophecy against the Philistines was given before Pharaoh smote Gaza, indicating a historical context of Egyptian military action.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 47:2, what imagery is used to describe the coming destruction?
options: Waters rising up out of the north like an overflowing flood
Fire consuming the land from the south
A great earthquake shaking the city
Darkness covering the land at noon
questions.correctAnswer: Waters rising up out of the north like an overflowing flood
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:2 uses the image of waters rising as an overflowing flood coming from the north to symbolize overwhelming destruction.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 47:3 describe as the cause of fear among the fathers and children of the land?
options: The noise of stamping hoofs, rushing chariots, and rumbling wheels
A plague sent by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The noise of stamping hoofs, rushing chariots, and rumbling wheels
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes the terrifying noise of horses and chariots as the cause of fear, emphasizing the military invasion bringing destruction.

questions.question: Jeremiah 47:4 mentions the cutting off of helpers from which two cities along with the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus and Zidon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:4 states that helpers will be cut off from Tyrus and Zidon, indicating the wide scope of destruction affecting allied cities.

questions.question: What condition is described in Jeremiah 47:5 regarding Gaza?
questions.correctAnswer: Baldness is come upon Gaza
questions.explanation: The phrase 'baldness is come upon Gaza' in verse 5 symbolizes devastation and mourning, reflecting the city's ruin.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 47:6, how is the sword of the LORD personified?
options: As a restless warrior needing to be put into its scabbard to rest
As a silent observer waiting patiently
As a shield protecting the innocent
As a burning fire that consumes endlessly
questions.correctAnswer: As a restless warrior needing to be put into its scabbard to rest
questions.explanation: Verse 6 uses personification by addressing the sword as if it can rest or be put away, emphasizing its active role in divine judgment.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage parallels the theme of divine judgment by flood imagery as seen in Jeremiah 47:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 8:7-8
questions.explanation: Isaiah 8:7-8 also uses the imagery of rising waters from the north to describe an invading force and divine judgment, paralleling Jeremiah 47:2.

questions.question: What is the significance of the north as the direction of the invading flood in Jeremiah 47:2 and 47:7?
options: The north was traditionally the direction from which Babylonian and Assyrian armies came
The north represents peace and safety
The north is the location of Jerusalem
The north was the land of the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: The north was traditionally the direction from which Babylonian and Assyrian armies came
questions.explanation: In biblical context, the north often symbolizes the direction of invading armies like Assyrians and Babylonians, indicating impending judgment as in Jeremiah 47:2 and 47:7.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 47:4, who will the LORD spoil along with the Philistines?
options: The remnant of the country of Caphtor
questions.correctAnswer: The remnant of the country of Caphtor
questions.explanation: Verse 4 specifies the remnant of Caphtor, traditionally identified with the Philistines' origin, will also be spoiled by the LORD.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew root meaning of the word translated as 'charge' in Jeremiah 47:7, and what does it imply about God's action?
options: The Hebrew word means 'command' or 'commission,' implying God intentionally appoints the sword to execute judgment
The Hebrew word means 'accident,' implying the sword acts randomly
The Hebrew word means 'mercy,' implying the sword is a protective force
The Hebrew word means 'peace,' implying the sword will bring calm
questions.correctAnswer: The Hebrew word means 'command' or 'commission,' implying God intentionally appoints the sword to execute judgment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term in Jeremiah 47:7 translated as 'charge' (Hebrew: 'tsavah') means a command or commission, indicating God's deliberate appointment of the sword as an agent of judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 47:5 use the image of 'baldness' in its literary device, and what does it symbolize?
options: Baldness symbolizes mourning and desolation, a metaphor for Gaza’s destruction
Baldness is used to show prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Baldness symbolizes mourning and desolation, a metaphor for Gaza’s destruction
questions.explanation: The use of 'baldness' in verse 5 is a metaphor expressing sorrow and ruin, common in Hebrew poetry as a sign of lamentation.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine judgment by a 'sword' as an instrument of God's wrath, similar to Jeremiah 47:6-7?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 19:15
questions.explanation: Revelation 19:15 describes a sword coming out of Christ’s mouth to judge nations, paralleling Jeremiah’s depiction of the sword as God's instrument of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 47:3 suggests that the fathers will look back to their children for strength during the invasion.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47:3 explicitly states the fathers will not look back to their children for strength due to feebleness of hands.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 47:4 indicates that the LORD’s judgment will also affect Tyrus and Zidon, not just the Philistines.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 4 clearly mentions that the LORD's day will spoil all the Philistines and cut off helpers from Tyrus and Zidon, showing a broader judgment.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 47 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will rise up out of the north before the destruction of the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: Waters
questions.explanation: The LORD states that 'waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood' indicating impending judgment (Jeremiah 47:2).

questions.question: What will happen to the inhabitants of the land when the flood rises?
questions.correctAnswer: They will cry and howl
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that 'then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl' (Jeremiah 47:2).

questions.question: What reason is given for the fathers not looking back to their children during the calamity?
questions.correctAnswer: Feebleness of hands
questions.explanation: The verse explains that 'the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands' (Jeremiah 47:3).

questions.question: What will happen to Tyrus and Zidon according to the prophecy?
options: They will be cut off from every helper
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cut off from every helper
questions.explanation: The prophecy states that the day comes to 'cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth' (Jeremiah 47:4).

questions.question: What condition is described as having come upon Gaza and Ashkelon?
questions.correctAnswer: Baldness
questions.explanation: The text specifies that 'Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off' (Jeremiah 47:5).

questions.question: What does the sword of the LORD symbolize in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment
questions.explanation: The sword of the LORD represents His judgment as it is described as having a charge against Ashkelon (Jeremiah 47:7).

questions.question: What question does the sword of the LORD ask in verse 6?
options: How long will you be quiet?
questions.correctAnswer: How long will you be quiet?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'O thou sword of the LORD, how long will it be ere thou be quiet?' (Jeremiah 47:6).

questions.question: What does this chapter reveal about God's sovereignty over nations?
questions.correctAnswer: He actively judges nations
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates God's sovereignty as He declares judgment on the Philistines, showing that He actively judges nations (Jeremiah 47:4-7).

questions.question: How does the prophecy against the Philistines connect to the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It signifies the end of all nations
It highlights God's justice against His enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights God's justice against His enemies
questions.explanation: This chapter highlights God's justice as He executes judgment against the Philistines, fitting into the narrative of God's righteousness (Jeremiah 47:4).

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 2 and 3 convey about human response to calamity?
options: People will cry out in despair
questions.correctAnswer: People will cry out in despair
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 indicate that as calamity strikes, people will cry and howl, showcasing despair (Jeremiah 47:2-3).

questions.question: What does God's promise to spoil the Philistines teach about His attribute of justice?
options: He is just and punishes evil
questions.correctAnswer: He is just and punishes evil
questions.explanation: The promise to spoil the Philistines indicates God's justice in punishing those who oppose Him (Jeremiah 47:4).

questions.question: What does the imagery of the overflowing flood signify in the context of God's judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: A destructive force of judgment
questions.explanation: The overflowing flood imagery signifies a destructive force that indicates God's impending judgment (Jeremiah 47:2).

questions.question: What role does the sword of the LORD play in the judgment on Ashkelon?
questions.correctAnswer: It executes judgment
questions.explanation: The sword is given a charge against Ashkelon, indicating its role in executing judgment (Jeremiah 47:7).

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God does not actively judge nations today. What does Jeremiah 47:4-7 actually teach?
options: God actively judges nations as a reflection of His justice
God is only concerned with individuals
questions.correctAnswer: God actively judges nations as a reflection of His justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 47 demonstrates that God actively judges nations, as seen in His judgment against the Philistines (Jeremiah 47:4-7).

questions.question: According to the chapter, what effect does the prophecy have on the cities of the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be in despair
questions.explanation: The chapter describes a situation of great despair as the cities face destruction and judgment (Jeremiah 47:5).
